title: Applied labs
description: Build, break, debug and evaluate in your own environment.

lessons.title: Lab: Graph modeling & construction
lessons.conceptOverview: Turn five documents into triples with source citations. Resolve two aliases and record an ambiguous entity without silently merging it.
lessons.whyItMatters: Combine entity relationships with semantic retrieval.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Property graphs represent nodes and edges with attributes; RDF represents triples. Ontologies define types and relationships. Extraction proposes entities and links, while entity resolution merges references to the same thing. Keep evidence and confidence on extracted claims rather than treating generated relationships as facts.

sections.title: 1. Establish a baseline
sections.content: Write down your inputs, expected behavior and constraints before starting. Turn five documents into triples with source citations. Resolve two aliases and record an ambiguous entity without silently merging it.

sections.title: 2. Introduce a failure
sections.content: Test the mistaken assumption: Extracted relationships are automatically verified facts. Record the observed result and the point where it diverges from your prediction.

sections.title: 3. Debug and evaluate
sections.content: Use the mechanism to explain the failure: Property graphs represent nodes and edges with attributes; RDF represents triples. Ontologies define types and relationships. Extraction proposes entities and links, while entity resolution merges references to the same thing. Keep evidence and confidence on extracted claims rather than treating generated relationships as facts. Change one variable at a time. Repeat the baseline and add a held-out case. Submit the implementation, results and limitations.

commonMistakes: Extracted relationships are automatically verified facts.
keyTakeaways: Property graphs represent nodes and edges with attributes; RDF represents triples.

lessons.title: Lab: Graph querying & hybrid search
lessons.conceptOverview: Design a two-hop query for people working at organizations funded by a named investor. Compare it with vector search and identify what each misses.
lessons.whyItMatters: Combine entity relationships with semantic retrieval.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Graph databases such as Neo4j support relationship traversal, often through Cypher. Traversal answers explicit structural questions; embeddings retrieve similar concepts. A hybrid pipeline can use vector candidates to find entry nodes, then traverse a bounded neighborhood. Limit depth and fanout to control cost and noise.

lessons.title: Lab: GraphRAG & evaluation
lessons.conceptOverview: Build a small graph-plus-vector retrieval benchmark. Include local fact questions and global summary questions; report quality and ingestion cost separately.
lessons.whyItMatters: Combine entity relationships with semantic retrieval.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: GraphRAG can retrieve connected evidence or summarize communities to answer broader corpus questions. Community detection groups densely connected nodes, but summaries can lose minority details. Evaluate multi-hop answers, provenance, extraction quality and index-update cost against a simpler RAG baseline.
